messages:
morgan: Hey team — hitting TLS errors in the Go SDK streaming path behind corp proxy. Root error: "tls: certificate signed by unknown authority". Non-streaming API calls are fine. curl works if I pass --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt. Any ideas?

jin: Did you try setting SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR? Go's x509 uses the system cert pool differently on some images.

morgan: We're running a static Go build (CGO_ENABLED=0) in a slim docker image. I installed ca-certificates and curl checks out, but the app still fails.

lina: If you're static (CGO_ENABLED=0) then Go uses the Go root cert pool which expects a PEM bundle at /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt (depends on distro). On alpine you often need ca-certificates package and sometimes to set SSL_CERT_FILE.

morgan: Could static linking be the reason streaming only fails? non-stream works though.

jin: Streaming likely uses HTTP/2 (h2) or websockets. The proxy could be intercepting h2 differently, re-signing with a corporate CA for those connections. Do an openssl s_client -connect against the streaming host and the non-stream host and compare cert chains.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: noting this issue — adding corp CA to common dev images as a temporary fix.

morgan: Ran openssl s_client -servername stream.api.redwood.internal -connect stream.api.redwood.internal:443 -showcerts. Response cert chain contains an internal CN=CorpProxy-Intercept root. So yep, MITM for that path only.

lina: That explains it. Workarounds: 1) Add the corp CA PEM to the container trust store (best for dev), 2) set SSL_CERT_FILE to point at the PEM bundle, 3) configure the SDK's TLS root pool manually, or 4) avoid proxy for those hosts (split-tunnel). Avoid skip-verify in prod.

jin: Example for Go SDK — load a cert pool and pass it to the transport:

```go
b, _ := os.ReadFile("/etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem")
pool := x509.NewCertPool()
pool.AppendCertsFromPEM(b)
tlsCfg := &tls.Config{RootCAs: pool}
tr := &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: tlsCfg}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```

If you use http2 directly, ensure http2.Transport's TLSClientConfig is set, and for gRPC use credentials.NewTLS(tlsCfg).

morgan: Nice. One more weirdness — when we tried mTLS (client cert) the server returned "bad certificate" intermittently. We discovered our PEM that concatenated certs was in wrong order (root first). Reordering to leaf -> intermediates fixed it.

lina: Yep, client cert chain order matters: leaf first, then intermediates. Also ensure the private key matches the cert (openssl x509 -noout -modulus ...). In some corp proxies SNI can be stripped; double-check SNI hostnames because some endpoints are virtual-hosted.

jin: Also note that static Go builds may not pick up OS stores on some distros. If you want to keep static builds, explicitly set SSL_CERT_FILE at runtime or embed the PEM in your image. We should add a short note in devex about this.

morgan: I'll paste a minimal repro and logs in this thread shortly. Plan: add corp CA to dev images, update Go SDK docs with TLS config snippet and SSL_CERT_FILE tip, and add a quick checklist for mTLS (order, key match, SNI). Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

lina: Thanks — ping me if you want me to run a quick test image locally.
